newsitem.title: JAMAICA: CRICKET-MONGIA RESCUES INDIA AFTER ROSE STRIKES.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-MONGIA RESCUES INDIA AFTER ROSE STRIKES.

text.p: Wicketkeeper Nayan Mongia came to India's rescue on Saturday after West Indies paceman Franklyn Rose, making his test debut, had ripped through the middle order, taking four wickets in seven overs.

Rose, who added a fifth wicket to his tally in the final session, took all four wickets in the morning as India, beginning the third day of the first test at 108 for one, slumped to 155 for five at lunch.
But Mongia, helped by Saurav Ganguly, averted any threat of a follow-on with a knock of 74 not out, taking India to 308 for seven at the close in reply to West Indies' total of 427 all out.
Mongia and Ganguly batted through the afternoon to give India a reasonable chance of salvaging a draw after the morning session had left them in a difficult position.
The tourists added 19 runs in the first 50 minutes of the day before Rose claimed his first victim when he bowled opener Vangipurappu Laxman for 64.
Rose also claimed the wickets of Rahul Dravid (43), captain Sachin Tendulkar (seven) and Mohammad Azharuddin (five) but then saw Ganguly dropped by wicketkeeper Junior Murray just before lunch.

Murray's mistake prove costly as Ganguly and Mongia went on to add 81 runs, batting with increasing confidence on a fairly slow and low pitch. They survived two scares through misunderstandings which nearly left Mongia stranded.
Shortly after tea, Ganguly became Rose's fifth and final victim of the day when he was caught by Brian Lara for 42 with the total at 234. Rose finished with figures of five for 79.
Fourteen runs were added before Anil Kumble was bowled by Ian Bishop for seven but Sunil Joshi, 23 not out, and Mongia batted through the rest of the day, adding 59 more runs in the process.
